title: The effect of speech masking on the human subcortical response to continuous speech
description: EEG dataset of auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) recorded from 25 normal-hearing adults listening to continuous peaky speech from one to five simultaneous male talkers, plus click trains. It was collected to examine how speech masking affects subcortical neural encoding of naturally uttered speech. Speech conditions were clean, 0 dB, -3 dB and -6 dB SNR.
methods_description: Participants sat in a darkened sound-isolating booth and rested or watched silent captioned videos while EEG was recorded in BrainVision format. Stimuli were presented at 65 dB SPL per story through ER-2 insert earphones and an RME Babyface Pro sound card, controlled with custom expyfun Python scripts. Stimuli were 10-minute randomized 40 Hz click trains and 30 minutes of peaky speech per SNR condition, with story files randomized. Trigger codes marked trial onset and trial identity.
